notes: Split sex:0 - it fans out to output (0) and node 155.
Split fbs:0 - it fans out to output (0) and node 155.

Split hidden node 155 - it fans out to output (0) and node 534. Copy 155_a feeds the output, 155_b feeds node 534. This enables clean coverage of both the benign_profile_gate and the 534 risk-aggregation node.
Split exang:0 - feeds both 155_a (output-side gate) and 155_b (534-side gate).

params.name: benign_profile_gate

payload.interpretation: benign-profile gate: activates for female patients with no exercise-induced angina; normal fasting glucose slightly attenuates. Lowers predicted risk.

records.narrative: Closed-form gate. A shallow, single-step gate encoding a recognised protective factor (female + no exertional angina).
Activation profile verified on the test split: active for ~70% of patients, hard-zero for ~30%. A genuinely used gate, not a dead or saturated unit.

payload.description: Disable the 155_a->0 readout (undo annotation layer, disable_connection, recompute)

records.narrative: The single largest nonlinear contribution to generalisation: removing this gate costs 0.028 test AUC. A shallow protective-factor gate that genuinely generalises. Re-verified on the full test split.

params.hypothesis: Node 155_a computes a 'benign profile' gate: 155_a = ReLU(0.824*sex:0 + 1.109*exang:0 - 0.509*fbs:0 + 0.088). Activates for female patients (sex:0=1) with no exertional angina (exang:0=1); normal fasting glucose slightly attenuates. Output-facing copy of hidden node 155. Activation profile: active 70% / hard-zero 30% (verified). Reads out to output with weight -0.960, lowering predicted risk. Ablation: removing this readout drops test AUC 0.897->0.869 (-0.028) - the single largest nonlinear contribution to generalisation.

params.name: benign_profile_gate_534path

payload.readout: 155_b -> 534, weight +0.818; net path effect through 534 = +0.818 * -0.884 = -0.72 per unit
payload.interpretation: second, bit-identical copy of the benign gate, routed into the 534 aggregation gate instead of the output - the benign signal is encoded twice

records.narrative: 155_b shares incoming weights and bias 0.088 with 155_a exactly (bit-identical). The benign protective signal is therefore redundantly encoded twice - once direct to output, once inside the 534 gate. Redundant double-encoding is a symptom of the same overfitting the 534 gate exhibits.

params.hypothesis: Node 155_b computes the SAME benign-profile gate as 155_a (identical incoming weights and bias 0.088); it is the second copy of hidden node 155, routed into node 534 instead of the output. The benign signal is therefore encoded twice - once directly to the output (155_a) and once inside the 534 gate (155_b). 155_b enters 534 with weight +0.818; net path effect (+0.818)*(-0.884) = -0.72 per unit, same risk-lowering direction as the direct copy.

params.name: chol_threshold

payload.readout: 3040 -> 534, weight -0.677; net path effect +0.60 per unit (high cholesterol raises risk)
payload.interpretation: one-sided cholesterol threshold; since chol is z-normalised, turns on only above ~0.82 SD above the mean

records.narrative: A sparse one-sided cholesterol threshold - the sub-unit that lets cholesterol act as a risk factor only above a level rather than linearly. But it sits inside the 534 gate, which ablation shows contributes nothing on test.

payload.interpretation: sparse threshold detector - fires only for the ~17.5% of patients well above average cholesterol

records.narrative: Activation profile verified: fires for only ~17.5% of patients, confirming a sparse one-sided threshold detector rather than a linear response.

params.hypothesis: Node 3040 = ReLU(1.052*chol - 0.864): a one-sided cholesterol threshold. Since cholesterol is z-normalised, this turns on only above ~0.82 SD above the mean. Activation profile: hard-zero 82.5% / active 17.5% (verified) - a sparse threshold detector. Feeds node 534 with -0.677; net path effect +0.60 per unit (high cholesterol raises predicted risk). This is the sub-unit that lets cholesterol act as a risk factor only above a level rather than linearly - but it sits inside the 534 gate, which the ablation shows contributes nothing on test.

params.name: restbp_chol_interaction

payload.interpretation: near-linear resting-blood-pressure signal - 3240 is a linear pass-through (always-on), 2379 near-always-on; higher resting BP raises risk

records.narrative: Despite the two-node structure this collapses to a near-linear resting-BP term: 3240 is always-on (a pass-through, not a gate) and 2379 is near-always-on. A shallow, generalising risk term.

payload.interpretation: 3240 100% active confirms it is a linear pass-through, not a gate

records.narrative: Activation profile verified: 3240 is 100% active - confirming it is a linear pass-through rather than a gate, which is why the whole pathway reduces to a near-linear resting-BP term.

payload.description: Disable the 2379->0 readout, recompute on test split

records.narrative: A modest but real generalising contribution: removing the resting-BP term costs 0.012 test AUC. Re-verified on the test split.

params.hypothesis: Subgraph {trestbps, chol_c, 3240, 2379}: a near-linear resting-blood-pressure signal. 3240 = ReLU(0.978*trestbps + 3.4) is always-on (100% active, verified) - a linear pass-through, not a gate. 2379 = ReLU(0.931*3240 - 0.529*chol_c - 0.754) simplifies to ReLU(0.911*trestbps - 0.529*chol_c + 2.41), near-always-on. Reads out to output with +0.364 (higher resting BP raises risk). Ablation: removing this readout drops test AUC 0.897->0.885 (-0.012) - a modest but real generalising contribution.

params.name: risk_aggregation_gate

payload.interpretation: the model's most elaborate unit - a genuine ReLU gate composing vessel count, a cholesterol copy, the cholesterol threshold, and the redundant benign copy; when the benign signal is strong the whole block clips off together

records.narrative: Composed closed form (the composition annotation resolves into its two children plus two direct inputs). On paper the model's most sophisticated structure - a rectified gate folding four risk signals together. Signs match cardiology.

payload.interpretation: a genuine gate - silent for just over half of patients

records.narrative: Activation profile verified: hard-zero for 53.5% of patients, confirming 534 is a genuine gate rather than a pass-through.

payload.diagnosis: train-only / overfit - the showpiece unit slightly HELPS test when removed while costing on train; fit to the 242 training cases alone
payload.description: Disable the 534->0 readout, recompute on both splits (undo annotation layer, disable_connection, recompute, restore)

records.narrative: KEY RESULT. The model's most elaborate structure does no real work on held-out data: removing it changes test AUC by +0.002 (slightly helps) while costing on train. Structural elaboration is where the overfitting concentrates. Only holding structure against ablation reveals it - the gate looks like the centrepiece, yet measurement shows it is decorative while the plainest gates do the work. Re-verified on both splits.

params.hypothesis: Node 534 = ReLU(0.818*[benign_profile_gate_534path] - 0.677*[chol_threshold] - 1.155*ca - 0.592*chol - 0.761): the model's most elaborate unit, a genuine ReLU gate (hard-zero 53.5% verified) composing four risk signals - vessel count (ca), a cholesterol copy, the cholesterol threshold (3040), and the redundant benign-profile copy (155_b). Net per-unit output effects: ca +1.02, chol +0.52, chol_threshold +0.60, benign -0.72; when the benign signal is strong the whole block is clipped off together. KEY ABLATION RESULT: disabling 534's readout changes test AUC only 0.897->0.899 (+0.002) while train drops 0.946->0.942 - i.e. this showpiece unit is essentially train-only and does not generalise. Signs match cardiology but the structure is fit to the 242 training cases.

params.name: heart_disease_risk_score

records.narrative: Whole-model performance and coverage. Complete structural and compositional coverage reached with 8 node splits and ZERO function-changing operations - the explained network is computationally identical to the trained one. Wider generalisation gap (0.049 AUC) on the small 61-row test split.

payload.conclusion: the two simple gates (benign, restbp) carry all the generalising benefit; the elaborate 534 aggregation gate is train-only
payload.description: Full ablation ladder, test AUC, baseline 0.897 (re-verified on test split today)

records.narrative: Full ablation ladder, re-verified end-to-end on the test split. Nonlinearity as a whole buys +0.037 test AUC, but the benefit comes almost entirely from the two shallow gates encoding recognised protective/risk factors. The elaborate composed gate contributes nothing on held-out data. A complete explanation doubles as a diagnosis of how much nonlinear structure earns its place.

params.hypothesis: Root: y0 = ReLU(bias 0.318 + linear core + 3 nonlinear pathways). (1) DIRECT LINEAR CORE of 17 inputs to the output - ca (largest, +2.03), cp:4 (+1.21), slope:2, chol, cp:2, oldpeak push risk up; sex:0 (-0.71), slope:1, thalach push down. By SHAP the top drivers are ca, cp:4, sex:0, slope:2, chol. (2) benign_profile_gate (155_a, -0.96) lowers risk for females without exertional angina. (3) restbp_chol_interaction (2379, +0.364). (4) risk_aggregation_gate (534, -0.884), the elaborate composed unit. 7 features unused. PERFORMANCE: train AUC 0.946 / test 0.897. ABLATION LADDER (test AUC, baseline 0.897): linear-core only 0.860 (nonlinearity buys +0.037); remove benign gate -0.028; remove restbp -0.012; remove 534 gate +0.002. So the two simple gates (benign, restbp) carry all the generalising benefit; the elaborate 534 aggregation gate is train-only. The benign signal is redundantly encoded twice (155_a direct + 155_b inside 534).
